source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
finding: Asking one call for k candidates with verbalized probabilities (a structural diverge step) raises diversity over direct prompting and over a sequence baseline at the same number of total responses. Gains are larger for bigger models.
numbers: Creative writing, 100 prompts per task, N=30 samples, k=5. Diversity 1.6-2.1x over direct. Human diversity rating (1-4), Direct/Sequence/VS-Standard: poem 1.90/2.07/2.39, story 2.74/2.76/3.06, joke 1.83/2.93/3.01. Models: GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5, Claude-4-Sonnet, Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen3-235B, o3, R1. Larger models gain 1.5-2x more.
limits: Budget matched by number of responses (direct N calls, VS ceil(N/k) calls), not by tokens; latency and token cost not given. Quality judged by Claude-3.7-Sonnet. Human agreement on poem diversity only 0.54. Quality drops if k is too large; small models lose quality.
agent_relevance: Best current evidence that a structural candidate-set step beats plain sampling for 2025 frontier models at equal response count. Supports a code-set diverge step as a batch-of-k call. Does not answer token parity.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: reasoning models (o3, DeepSeek-R1) and synthetic math data, appendix tables
finding: Reasoning-trained models also collapse under direct prompting (low diversity), and the verbalized-candidates step lifts them strongly. Using diverse generation to build math training data raised downstream accuracy.
numbers: Poem diversity, direct to VS-CoT: R1 12.4 to 33.6; o3 13.2 to 28.0. Story: R1 24.8 to 49.0; o3 25.6 to 40.2. Open QA coverage-N: R1 0.15 to 0.73; o3 0.11 to 0.71. Quality roughly flat (R1 story 63.0 to 58.2, o3 70.7 to 71.5). Synthetic data, mean accuracy over MATH500, OlympiadBench, Minerva: direct 30.6, CoT 33.7, sequence 34.3, multi-turn 33.2, VS-Standard 36.1, VS-CoT 36.9, VS-Multi 37.5.
limits: No non-reasoning twin of o3 or R1 in the same tables, so it cannot say reasoning models are worse than their base. Math result is about generating training data, not solving problems with a diverge stage. Appendix cost numbers not given.
agent_relevance: Closes part of gap 10: reasoning models are not exempt from homogeneity and respond to the same structural fix. Gap 2 only touched indirectly (diversity helps data for closed tasks).

source: Jiang et al. (2025/2026) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (Infinity-Chat)
finding: Single-stage sampling from 25 to 42 models gives highly similar answers inside a model and across models, even with hot sampling. Diversity-oriented decoding (min-p, temperature 2.0) only reduces it a little.
numbers: 26K open-ended queries, 6 categories and 17 subcategories, 31,250 human annotations (25 raters per item). Same-prompt average pairwise embedding similarity usually above 0.8 at top-p 0.9, T 1.0. With min-p (T 2.0): 81% of response pairs above 0.7 and 61.2% above 0.8. Cross-model average similarity 0.71-0.82 (DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82; DeepSeek-V3 vs gpt-4o 0.81). Mean similarity high open-endedness 0.800 vs low 0.837 (42 models). 'Write a metaphor about time': 25 models x 50 responses fall in two clusters (river, weaver).
limits: Embedding similarity is a proxy for diversity; English WildChat prompts only; authors do not test multi-stage scaffolds or code-set pipelines; causes of cross-model similarity unknown.
agent_relevance: Strong reason to make diversification structural and not rely on temperature. Cross-model mixing gives limited gain because models agree (gap 9 mostly negative for plain mixing; scaffold effect still untested).

source: Jiang et al. (2025/2026) Artificial Hivemind: judges and reward models vs 25 human raters
finding: LLM judges, reward models and LMs agree less with humans exactly where it matters for creative selection: among similar-quality answers and where raters disagree.
numbers: Correlations between model and human scores drop 'significantly' on the subsets of similar-quality pairs (top 60-95% most similar) and on high-entropy items (top 2-16% by Shannon entropy over 25 labels), for both absolute and pairwise setups. Exact r values are in figures, not read.
limits: Quality ratings, not originality ratings. Exact coefficients not extracted. Judge family not isolated.
agent_relevance: A code-set converge stage that uses an LLM critic should expect weak ranking among near-equal candidates; use diversity rules (dedup, coverage) rather than a scalar critic score.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) AI Delivers Creative Output but Struggles with Thinking Processes
finding: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o beat humans on divergent and convergent output tasks but show human-unlike evaluation: no novelty-appropriateness trade-off in GPT-4 and GPT-4o, and worse choice of the most creative idea for GPT-4o.
numbers: Exp 7: humans r=-0.39 (p=.002) and GPT-3.5 r=-0.67 between novelty and appropriateness weights; GPT-4 r=0.13 (p=.310), GPT-4o r=0.16 (p=.196). GPT-3.5 rated all dimensions higher than humans (p<.001); GPT-4 rated novelty higher than humans (p=.003) and appropriateness lower (p=.008). Exp 8: 64 humans and 64 runs per model chose the most creative of 12 ideas, 4 items; humans had lower decision error than GPT-4o, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 not significantly different. Also lower forward flow than humans in free and chain association.
limits: Chinese participants, small stimulus sets (24 and 48 ideas), no scaffold; one-shot LLM raters. Not tested with a critic prompt that separates novelty from appropriateness.
agent_relevance: Supports gap 4: a single LLM critic does not weigh novelty and fit like people. Score novelty and validity as separate calls (or separate rubrics) and combine in code.

source: Ma, Grandi et al. (2024) Exploring the Capabilities of LLMs for Generating Diverse Design Solutions
finding: With GPT-4, diversity did not rise monotonically with temperature or top-P; the best was temperature 1, top-P 1. A one-extra-step critique-and-edit prompt gave the largest diversity gain among 8 prompt methods. No LLM method beat human crowd diversity.
numbers: 4,000 GPT-4 solutions, 5 design topics, 8 temperature/top-P combos (high-high excluded as incoherent), 8 prompt methods, 4 diversity metrics (DPP, nearest sample, convex hull, centroid distance; Spearman between metrics mostly strong); compared with 100 crowd (MTurk) solutions per topic. 50 solutions per condition. The adjective 'unique' gave lower diversity than 'creative' or 'novel'; a persona 'excellent at far-fetched ideas' gave a 'considerable' gain. A linear classifier separated LLM from human solutions perfectly, but human-from-LLM varied by topic.
limits: Percent differences only in heatmaps, no tests; 50 solutions per cell; GPT-4 (2024); the critique step adds tokens so there is no token parity.
agent_relevance: Temperature is an unreliable diversity dial for GPT-4; an extra critique-edit pass beat it. Supports gap 3 for a 2024 frontier model and gap 5 (a second pass helps), without token control.

source: Divergent-Convergent Thinking in LLMs for Creative Problem Generation (CreativeDC, arXiv 2512.23601)
finding: Two-phase prompt (brainstorm ignoring the required concepts, then pick one and tie it to the concepts, retry if it fails) beats Base and CoT on diversity and novelty with a small utility cost. No token count and no ablation of either phase is reported.
numbers: Qwen3-235B-A22B, T 1.0, 20 contexts x 100 problems. No persona: LexDiv 0.81 vs 0.74/0.75; SemDiv 0.54 vs 0.46/0.46; SemNov 0.30 vs 0.20/0.18; utility 90.85 vs 92.95/91.35 (%). With persona SemNov 0.31 vs 0.22/0.23. Vendi +24.0% vs CoT at K=10, +72.0% at K=100. Semantic novelty +51.5% over Base, +63.5% over CoT.
limits: Confirms the critique weak spot: no parity and no ablation. One generator; Python problems; utility by LLM judge and tests; novelty measured against other methods' outputs.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open for compute parity; the design (generate with constraints hidden, then bind) is a usable template for a code-set diverge stage.

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (CHI)
finding: Humans shown AI-generated images while sketching fixated more on a given example than the no-support group, and on the AI images themselves ('fixation displacement'). Variety fell; originality was unchanged.
numbers: N=60 between subjects, 20 per condition, 20-minute chatbot-avatar sketching, example with 14 features. Design fixation score: GenAI .32 (89% CI .11-.54, BF 124); image search .27 (BF 42.48). Fluency: image search -.49 (BF 46.62), GenAI -.21. Variety: image search -.40, GenAI -.29. Originality: GenAI -.03, image search -.01. 117 prompts: 44% reused brief words; 206 of 468 images (44%) humanoid robots. Sketch fixation vs preceding AI image fixation rho=.56.
limits: Humans, not models; image tool; novice sample; short task.
agent_relevance: Shows that stimuli shown in the generate phase narrow people. Gap 6 is about the model itself seeing stimuli; this is the human-side counterpart, so the risk for a pipeline is cross-contamination between stage outputs.

source: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI (arXiv 2502.05870)
finding: Designers using ChatGPT (GPT-4o) and Midjourney produced less diverse chair designs than award entries and most noticed repetition.
numbers: N=10 designers, 96 GenAI solutions. Text novelty proportion ChatGPT 67.4% vs Red Dot 78.2%; unique words 180 vs 312 (86 shared). Image distance global features 16.25 vs 16.05 (p=.024), shape, colour, texture p<.01. 7 of 10 saw text repetition, 8 of 10 image repetition. Nearly all pasted ChatGPT prompts into Midjourney unchanged.
limits: Tiny N, uncontrolled baseline (105 award entries), one domain, authors call it preliminary.
agent_relevance: Homogeneity is visible to users, yet people adopt it; a scaffold should enforce novelty checks in code, not trust the user or model.

source: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity (arXiv 2504.05228)
finding: 20 leading models give much less diversity than human writers; larger models in a family are often less diverse than smaller ones; in-context regeneration (asking again with earlier answers shown) raises diversity.
numbers: 20 models. No further numbers on the abstract page read.
limits: Abstract only; effect sizes of regeneration not read.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence for gap 6: showing earlier outputs plus an instruction to differ helped, not hurt, so fixation by shown candidates is not automatic for LLMs. Needs a direct test.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Generate several thoughts per step, evaluate them with the model, and search: this solves a closed task that straight chain of thought mostly fails.
numbers: Game of 24 with GPT-4: chain-of-thought 4% solved, Tree of Thoughts 74%.
limits: Abstract only; breadth, node counts and token cost not read, so no parity; one narrow puzzle.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: a diverge-and-evaluate loop helps on a closed verifiable task, but with a verifiable evaluator and many more calls. It is search, not a creativity prompt.

source: CreativityPrism (arXiv 2510.20091) cross-domain evaluation of LLM creativity
finding: Creativity scores do not transfer across tasks; novelty often correlates weakly or negatively with other metrics; frontier models do not lead on divergent thinking.
numbers: 17 LLMs, 8 tasks, 3 domains (divergent thinking, creative writing, logical reasoning), 3 dimensions (quality, novelty, diversity). Frontier models lead open models by about 0.10 (15%) in creative writing and logical reasoning, no significant lead in divergent thinking.
limits: Abstract page only. Does not separate reasoning models from non-reasoning ones in what was read.
agent_relevance: Do not infer closed-task benefit from open-task diversity gains (gap 2); measure per task. Gap 10 not answered here.

source: Automated Creativity Evaluation of Language Models Across Open-Ended Tasks (arXiv 2606.11762)
finding: A retrieval-based LLM judge agrees better with human consensus than ChatEval, and semantic entropy agrees better than cosine similarity, Self-BLEU or Distinct-n.
numbers: Tasks MacGyver, HypoGen, BookMIA, 300 problems each. Kappa with humans (MacGyver, 50 problems, 3 annotators): semantic entropy .56, cosine .49, Self-BLEU .35, Distinct-1 .37, Distinct-2 .34. Judge accuracy MacGyver 84.7% vs ChatEval 76.7%; BookMIA 83.0% vs 73.3% (BookMIA annotator kappa about .22). Tokens per pair: 23,758 in / 3,796 out vs 66,944 / 8,634 (about 63% fewer).
limits: Accuracy against study consensus labels; judge is an LLM; models not named on the page; no ablation; effects of reasoning, size, temperature stated in the abstract only.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: semantic entropy is a cheap code-side diversity measure; LLM judges are still weak on low-agreement domains.

source: Search snippet: GenSelect and best-of-N selectors for math (arXiv 2504.16891, 2507.17797)
finding: Selecting among several sampled solutions with a trained comparative selector beats majority voting on math.
limits: Search snippet only; trained selector, not a prompting scaffold.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 baseline: best-of-N with a selector is the strong equal-call competitor for closed tasks; no one has compared it with diverge-then-converge prompting.

source: Search snippet: structured pipelines against fixation (NexusAI arXiv 2604.10575; Conversational Agents as Catalysts 2406.11125)
finding: Authors argue plain chat output pushes users to converge early and propose a structured abstraction-and-decomposition pipeline.
agent_relevance: Possible later read for gaps 5 and 6.

source: Search snippet: brain-alignment preprint on reasoning-trained models and creative geometry (paper not identified)
finding: A search summary says a reasoning-trained variant shows the opposite brain-alignment pattern, suggesting chain-of-thought training moves representations away from creative structure.
limits: Second-hand summary of an unidentified paper; do not use.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open for behaviour; no direct measurement of reasoning vs base on divergence found.

source: Search log: incubation / context reset and interleaved-schedule searches in LLMs
finding: The arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned HTTP 429 and the shared WebSearch budget ran out, so gaps 5, 7 and 8 got no new primary source this session.
numbers: No papers found for an LLM incubation analogue or an interleaved-versus-single-cycle schedule test.
limits: Absence of evidence comes from a failed search, not a confirmed gap in the literature.
agent_relevance: Keep gaps 5, 7 and 8 open; run them as agent_test experiments.
